name: TeamStarWolf - Insider Threat
description: Curated practitioner view, not an official MITRE mapping. Scores are membership tiers (core=100, supporting=55), not severity, confidence, incident frequency, or a coverage guarantee. Technique IDs and tactic assignments are checked against official Enterprise ATT&CK 16.1 and the bundled 18.1 dataset; the layer retains v16-compatible tactic slugs. Selected abuse of granted access, information collection, unauthorized export, record manipulation, and sabotage. This is an independent selection informed by the library's insider-risk reference, not a reproduction of CTID's case dataset or its frequency rankings. A behavior match is not proof of malicious intent or insider identity; use authorization, business context, and privacy-aware review.

Create Account. Core: Creating accounts outside the approved lifecycle can preserve access or support fraudulent activity.
Data from Information Repositories. Core: Information repositories can supply sensitive records within an insider's legitimate reach.
Data from Local System. Core: Local data can be collected for an unauthorized purpose even when ordinary read access is permitted.
Data from Network Shared Drive. Core: Shared drives can enable bulk collection across documents available to a role.
Local Data Staging. Core: Local staging can consolidate data before an unauthorized transfer.
Archive via Utility. Core: Archive utilities can package collected data; compression alone is not an insider-risk finding.
Exfiltration over USB. Core: USB storage can carry data out of an environment without a network transfer.
Stored Data Manipulation. Core: Unauthorized changes to stored business records can support fraud or undermine integrity.
Data Destruction. Core: Destruction of data within an account's reach can cause sabotage; distinguish it from approved retention workflows.
File and Directory Discovery. Supporting: Directory browsing can help locate information outside the task's business need.
Screen Capture. Supporting: Screen capture can collect information that ordinary file-export controls do not cover.
Remote Email Collection. Supporting: Mailbox access can expose communications for unauthorized collection.
Email Forwarding Rule. Supporting: Unauthorized forwarding rules can sustain email collection; this technique is classified as collection, not exfiltration.
Data from Cloud Storage. Supporting: Granted cloud-storage access can expose business data to unauthorized collection.
Exfiltration to Cloud Storage. Supporting: Uploads to an unapproved cloud-storage destination can export collected data.
Transfer Data to Cloud Account. Supporting: Cloud-native sharing or copying to another account can move data outside its intended boundary.
File Deletion. Supporting: Deleting artifacts can conceal earlier activity; unlike data destruction, this row models evidence removal.
Disable or Modify Tools. Supporting: A privileged user can impair monitoring to conceal activity; planned maintenance must be distinguished.
Service Stop. Supporting: Unauthorized service stops can disrupt operations using otherwise legitimate administration.
Account Access Removal. Supporting: Removing account access can lock legitimate operators out of their systems.
Data Encrypted for Impact. Supporting: A privileged insider could encrypt accessible data for impact; this is a scenario extension, not a CTID case-frequency claim.

metadata.name: selection_rule
metadata.value: Core: account abuse, role-accessible collection, staging, USB export, stored-record manipulation and data destruction. Supporting: selected discovery, additional collection/export channels, concealment and availability effects. Parent techniques do not imply that every sub-technique is selected.

metadata.name: score_meaning
metadata.value: 100=core; 55=supporting. Membership only, not severity, prevalence, confidence, or measured defensive coverage.

metadata.name: tactic_policy
metadata.value: Display each selected technique under all of its official 16.1 tactics, verified to match the bundled snapshot. Display expansion does not assert a scenario uses every tactic or requires every step. The app may translate retired IDs for its newer live matrix.

metadata.name: validation_source
metadata.value: Official Enterprise ATT&CK 16.1 and src/assets/data/enterprise-attack.json (collection version 18.1). The bundled file is not v16; both snapshots retain defense-evasion.

metadata.value: INSIDER_THREAT_REFERENCE.md; selection and rationale are practitioner interpretation, not an official mapping.
